x: The highlights of the race from the Club's point of view was the excellent running of John Burr, who at his first attempt at this distance did the very creditable time of 1.27.22.

The individual race was won easily by "Lofty" Holden, of Cambridge H., and our first man home was Bob Taylor, 17th, our other scorers being Mick Porter, 27; John Burr, 32; Ray Tooby, 38; Len Bishop, 57, and George Stace, 61.
…aces after a lapse of 14 years, and just shows what can be done with properly applied training methods. Eddie Short and John Burr also ran quite well, and our scoring team was completed by Chas.…

John Burr, 99th, Alan Bishop, 219th, and Len Bishop 247th, completed our team, and but for the backward position of the latter two, we should have stood a good chance of once again winning the “ Charles Otway ” Cup, which is awarded to the first club finishing its complete team, outside the three placed clubs.

Archie Bedford was first home in the British Workers' 5 miles c.c. championship, with Ron Mitchell in second place. John Burr won the L.B.H. Novices c.c. race, and Eric Bishop was second in the Inter-Banks Junior event.
Gordon was 3rd, with Ron Morrell 5th in the Senior 100 and John Burr and Archie Bedford were 3rd and 4th in the 1 mile, which was won in 4 mins. 25 secs. by Brian Hewson, of Mitcham.
The 1½ miles run saw "Lofty" Holden in the field as a "guest" runner, and he won in 6 mins. 54 secs. from Archie Bedford, with John Burr third.

Bob Taylor was 2nd in the 1 mile, with John Burr 3rd, and George Stace ran well to win the 2 miles run in 9 mins. 58 secs. We also won the 1 miles medley relay, with Jim Heathfield, Bob Wolton, Ron Morrell and Ivan Mayers.
In the 1 mile, John Burr ran well to finish 2nd to Eddie Ellis, of T.V.H., while in the 880 yds. Bob Taylor was also 2nd to Don McMillan, the Australian Olympic runner.
We also turned out a team for the 2 mile team race at the same meeting and were again placed 3rd, our team being Jack Brown, Chas. Walker, Bill Lucas and John Burr.
Walker and John Burr, and although Chas. took the lead early on, once Gordon Pirie had gone by him he dropped back to finish outside the first six.

Walker ran well to retain this after dropping back at one stage and we then had John Burr doing the third leg. John made the pace for the first two laps, but once the leaders had gone by him he dropped back to hand over in 4th place to Peter Bagnall.
Gawler, John Burr, Peter Courtney, Eric Gebbett, and " Spud " Abbott, and all these were inside the 1st-class standard time of 15 mins. 45secs.
Walker was first home in 9 mins. 38 secs., with John Burr 3rd and Bill Lucas 5th, and they won the team event, beating Finchley and the Poly.

Arthur Bruce maintained this on the fourth as did Peter Bagnall and John Burr on stages 5 and 6. Chas Walker dropped a place on the long 7th relay but Len Bishop who ran very well, took us back into 2nd place on the 8th leg.Eddie Short and Bob Taylor maintained this position on the two final stages…
We were accompanied by members of the L.O.A.C. who travelled with our party both ways and John Burr spent a good evenings entertainment with them learning to play cards.

John Burr, once more in action after a leg injury, finished 3rd in the three miles in one of his best times which augurs well for a good winter season and in this race we also had Alan Bishop, Edmunds and Tom Carter, this having become a weekly effort for Tom - just like old times.

The 9th stage had been given to John Burr running in his first Brighton and so well did he run that he produced the best time of the day on this leg - definitely an encouraging start to what should be a long career on the Brighton Road.
John Burr 5th, gave us a good start. 6th was Johnny Butley, first man home for Surrey A.C. and then four more Bels., Masters, Tooby Trower and Bagnall.
John Burr and Dave Hooper, both rather unfit, ran extremely even laps but were unabe to get into the running and Jim was breathing down Dave's neck when the final whistle blew.
The best feature of the race was the expected tussle between Jack Brown, John Burr and Cliff Roffey, and an exciting battle it was with the three of them coming home within 2 seconds of each other.

We were unfortunate in having John Burr as a spectator but he had recently had a bad attack of flu' and was not fit to race. Colin Collis did well to complete the course as he too had a bad cold, but the "twelve"cup was at stake.
John Burr paddled to victory ahead of Eddie Paterson. Support by sprinters and middle distance men alike in the field events kept the result of the match in the balance right up to the end.
John Burr on stage 10 was obviously unfit but our position remained 6th. The final stage was taken by Arthur Bruce and was virtually just a formality for there was no one close in front or behind.
